symbols.name: source ring
symbols.meaning: The ring from which the ring homomorphism $\varphi$ starts.
symbols.quote: A ring homomorphism is a map $\varphi: Q \to Q'$ between two rings that preserves both operations, so that $\varphi(\xi+\eta)=\varphi(\xi)+\varphi(\eta)$ and $\varphi(\xi\eta)=\varphi(\xi)\varphi(\eta)$ for all $\xi,\eta\in Q$, and $\varphi(1)=1$.

symbols.name: target ring
symbols.meaning: The ring into which the ring homomorphism $\varphi$ sends elements of $Q$.
symbols.quote: A ring homomorphism is a map $\varphi: Q \to Q'$ between two rings that preserves both operations, so that $\varphi(\xi+\eta)=\varphi(\xi)+\varphi(\eta)$ and $\varphi(\xi\eta)=\varphi(\xi)\varphi(\eta)$ for all $\xi,\eta\in Q$, and $\varphi(1)=1$.

symbols.name: ring homomorphism
symbols.meaning: A map from the ring $Q$ to the ring $Q'$ that preserves sums, products and the identity.
symbols.quote: A ring homomorphism is a map $\varphi: Q \to Q'$ between two rings that preserves both operations, so that $\varphi(\xi+\eta)=\varphi(\xi)+\varphi(\eta)$ and $\varphi(\xi\eta)=\varphi(\xi)\varphi(\eta)$ for all $\xi,\eta\in Q$, and $\varphi(1)=1$.

symbols.name: ring element
symbols.meaning: An arbitrary element of the source ring $Q$.
symbols.quote: A ring homomorphism is a map $\varphi: Q \to Q'$ between two rings that preserves both operations, so that $\varphi(\xi+\eta)=\varphi(\xi)+\varphi(\eta)$ and $\varphi(\xi\eta)=\varphi(\xi)\varphi(\eta)$ for all $\xi,\eta\in Q$, and $\varphi(1)=1$.

symbols.name: ring element
symbols.meaning: A second arbitrary element of the source ring $Q$.
symbols.quote: A ring homomorphism is a map $\varphi: Q \to Q'$ between two rings that preserves both operations, so that $\varphi(\xi+\eta)=\varphi(\xi)+\varphi(\eta)$ and $\varphi(\xi\eta)=\varphi(\xi)\varphi(\eta)$ for all $\xi,\eta\in Q$, and $\varphi(1)=1$.

symbols.name: indeterminate
symbols.meaning: The variable of the example ring $Q=\mathbb{C}[w]/(w^2-1)$, whose square is $1$.
symbols.quote: Let $Q=\mathbb{C}[w]/(w^2-1)$, the ring in which the indeterminate $w$ satisfies $w^2=1$.

symbols.name: constant coefficient
symbols.meaning: The complex coefficient of $1$ in an element $\lambda+\mu w$ of $Q$.
symbols.quote: Every element of $Q$ has the form $\lambda+\mu w$ with $\lambda,\mu\in\mathbb{C}$, where $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are its coefficients.

symbols.name: linear coefficient
symbols.meaning: The complex coefficient of $w$ in an element $\lambda+\mu w$ of $Q$.
symbols.quote: Every element of $Q$ has the form $\lambda+\mu w$ with $\lambda,\mu\in\mathbb{C}$, where $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are its coefficients.

symbols.name: evaluation at one
symbols.meaning: The ring homomorphism from $Q$ to $\mathbb{C}$ that sends $w$ to $1$, which is not bijective.
